en.greeting: Welcome to C2! You already know the structures; now it's about control. Today: balanced lists and pairs, noun phrases a reader can follow, and sentences with only one meaning. Step by step.

steps.title: Parallel structure: the same form
steps.text: Lists read best when every item has the same shape.
steps.body:
**Parallel structure** = the items in a list or a pair have the **same grammatical form** (all verbs, all -ing forms, all nouns or all clauses).
- *The project aims to reduce costs, **improving** quality and **to train** staff.* ✗ (three shapes)
- *The project aims **to reduce** costs, **improve** quality and **train** staff.* ✓
Put *to* once at the start, or before every item; don't mix.
**Indonesian trap:** *mengurangi, meningkatkan, melatih* keep one shape by themselves. In English, choose the form for the first item and copy it.

pairs.en: The project aims to reduce costs, improve quality and train staff.
pairs.id: Proyek ini bertujuan mengurangi biaya, meningkatkan kualitas, dan melatih staf.

pairs.en: The project focuses on reducing costs, improving quality and training staff.
pairs.id: Proyek ini berfokus pada pengurangan biaya, peningkatan kualitas, dan pelatihan staf.

steps.title: Pairs that match
steps.text: Both halves of a pair need the same shape too.
steps.body: After **both … and**, **either … or**, **neither … nor**, **not only … but also**, the two halves match: *both demanding and well paid* ✓, not *both demanding and pays well* ✗. Comparisons with *than* too: *faster than driving*, not *than to drive*.

examples.en: The job is both demanding and well paid.
examples.id: Pekerjaan itu menuntut sekaligus bergaji bagus. (dua kata sifat)

examples.en: She not only wrote the code but also tested it.
examples.id: Dia tidak hanya menulis kodenya, tetapi juga mengujinya. (dua kata kerja)

examples.en: We can either meet in Bandung or talk online.
examples.id: Kita bisa bertemu di Bandung atau bicara secara online. (dua kata kerja)

examples.en: Neither the manager nor the staff knew about the audit.
examples.id: Baik manajer maupun stafnya tidak tahu soal audit itu. (dua kata benda)

examples.en: Taking the train is faster than driving.
examples.id: Naik kereta lebih cepat daripada menyetir. (-ing dan -ing)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pak Hasan is writing the aims of a new programme. Check every item after 'aims to'.

question.prompt: Which sentence has correct parallel structure?
options: The programme aims to support small farmers, cutting food waste and to create local jobs.
The programme aims to support small farmers, to cut food waste and creating local jobs.
The programme aims to support small farmers, cut food waste and create local jobs.
question.explanation: One *to* at the start, then three bare verbs: *support, cut, create*. The other two mix to + verb with an -ing form, so the list loses its shape.

steps.title: Unpack the noun stack
steps.text: One head noun, and only a few words in front of it.
steps.body:
**Recap (C1):** a noun phrase has one **head** (kata inti); the verb agrees with it.
A **noun stack** piles many nouns before the head: *the government new rural school teacher training funding policy* ✗
**Unpack it:** find the head (usually the last noun: *policy*), put the owner and an adjective before it, and move the details after it with *on / for / in / of* or one relative clause.
**Indonesian trap:** don't reverse the Indonesian order into a stack, and don't turn every *yang* into *which is*.

pairs.en: the government's new policy on funding teacher training in rural schools
pairs.id: kebijakan baru pemerintah tentang pendanaan pelatihan guru di sekolah-sekolah pedesaan

pairs.en: the hospital's plan to recruit more night-shift nurses
pairs.id: rencana rumah sakit untuk merekrut lebih banyak perawat shift malam

steps.title: Find the clearest version
steps.text: Bu Ani's report mentions 'the city council new street food vendor licence fee'.

question.prompt: Which is the clearest way to write 'the city council new street food vendor licence fee' in a report?
options: the city council's new licence fee for street food vendors
the new fee of the licence of the vendors of street food of the city council
the fee which is new which is for the licence which street food vendors need from the city council
question.explanation: Head = **fee**. The owner and the adjective go before it (*the city council's new licence fee*), the people after it (*for street food vendors*). The second is a chain of *of*, the third the *yang … yang …* translation: both bury the head.

steps.title: Four kinds of ambiguity
steps.text: Can your sentence be read in two ways? These are the usual causes.
steps.body:
**1. Dangling modifier:** *Walking into the office, the computer was already on* ✗ → *…, **I** saw that the computer was already on*.
**2. Misplaced only/almost:** they limit the word right after them. *We **almost lost** every client* (we lost none) ≠ *We lost **almost every** client* (we lost most).
**3. Unclear pronoun:** *When the manager met the consultant, **she** said …* Who? Repeat the noun.
**4. Unclear attachment:** *I saw the man **with the binoculars**.* Whose binoculars? → *Using binoculars, I saw the man.*

pairs.id: Hanya Rina yang menandatangani kontrak itu.
Rina hanya menandatangani kontrak itu, bukan dokumen lain.

pairs.en: When the manager met the consultant, the consultant said the budget was too small.
pairs.id: Saat manajer bertemu konsultan, konsultan itulah yang bilang anggarannya terlalu kecil.

steps.title: Whose laptop?
steps.text: Budi and Dimas are both men, so 'his' can point to either of them.

question.prompt: It was Dimas's laptop that crashed. Which sentence says this clearly?
options: Budi phoned Dimas because his laptop had crashed.
Dimas's laptop had crashed, so Budi phoned him.
Budi phoned Dimas because of his crashed laptop.
question.explanation: In the first and third, *his* can mean Budi's or Dimas's. The second names the owner (*Dimas's laptop*), and *him* can only be Dimas, because Budi is the one phoning.

steps.title: Put almost in its place
steps.text: almost limits the word right after it.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Dia (memang) mengirim laporan itu ke hampir semua mitra.
question.solution: She sent the report to almost every partner.
question.explanation: *almost every partner* = nearly all of the partners, and she really did send it. *She almost sent the report to every partner* would mean she didn't send it at all.

steps.title: Long sentences: build or split
steps.text: One sentence can hold four clauses, if it's built well.
steps.body:
Participle clause + **main clause** + relative clause + reason, all in one sentence (see the tile).
**Keep it clear:** main subject and verb early and close together; each extra clause next to what it describes; long, new information at the end; **parallel clauses** for parallel ideas (*why …, what … and how …*).
**Split it** when there are two main messages or the reader waits too long for the verb.
**Indonesian trap:** long *yang … dan … sehingga … di mana …* chains. *di mana* is only *where* for a place or situation.

pairs.en: Having reviewed the figures, the board approved the budget, which had been cut by 10%, because sales had risen.
pairs.id: Setelah meninjau angka-angkanya, dewan menyetujui anggaran, yang sudah dipotong 10%, karena penjualan naik.

steps.title: Balance the clauses
steps.text: After a two-month delay, the board wants a report. Look at the three things it should explain.

question.prompt: Which sentence keeps the clauses parallel?
options: The report should explain why the launch was delayed, our lessons and how to avoid delays in future.
The report should explain why the launch was delayed, what we learnt and how we will avoid delays in future.
The report should explain why the launch was delayed, what we learnt and avoiding delays in future.
question.explanation: All three things are **wh-clauses** with their own subject and verb: *why … was delayed, what we learnt, how we will avoid*. The first mixes in a noun phrase (*our lessons*) and *how to*; the third ends with an -ing form.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: The whole lesson on one page. Check these before you send a report.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Complex sentence control
artifact.intro: Parallel, readable, one meaning. A long sentence is fine if a reader can follow it the first time.
rows: to reduce costs, improving quality and to train staff
to reduce costs, improve quality and train staff
the government new rural school teacher training funding policy
the government's new policy on funding teacher training in rural schools
the app which is new which is from the startup which is in Bandung
the new app from a Bandung startup
Walking into the office, the computer was already on.
Walking into the office, I saw that the computer was already on.
We almost lost every client. (if you lost most)
Rina only signed the contract. (if you mean nothing else)
When the manager met the consultant, she said …
I saw the man with the binoculars.
Using binoculars, I saw the man.
The clinic, which a foundation whose director … funded, opened …
The clinic opened … It was funded by …
tips: Lists and pairs: choose the form for the first item and copy it.
Noun phrases: head early, one or two words before it, short phrases after it.
Before sending: who does each action, and what does each only, almost, she or which point to?

examples.en: Walking into the office, I saw that the computer was already on.
examples.id: Saat masuk ke kantor, saya melihat komputernya sudah menyala.

steps.text: Want more? These university writing-lab pages explain parallel structure and dangling modifiers with extra examples.

id.greeting: Selamat datang di C2! Kamu sudah mengenal strukturnya; sekarang soal kendali. Hari ini: daftar dan pasangan yang seimbang, noun phrase yang bisa diikuti pembaca, dan kalimat yang hanya punya satu arti. Langkah demi langkah.

steps.title: Struktur paralel: bentuk yang sama
steps.text: Daftar paling enak dibaca kalau semua bagiannya punya bentuk yang sama.
steps.body:
**Struktur paralel** = semua bagian dalam daftar atau pasangan punya **bentuk tata bahasa yang sama** (semuanya kata kerja, semuanya -ing, semuanya kata benda, atau semuanya klausa).
- *The project aims to reduce costs, **improving** quality and **to train** staff.* ✗ (tiga bentuk)
- *The project aims **to reduce** costs, **improve** quality and **train** staff.* ✓
Tulis *to* sekali di awal, atau di depan setiap bagian; jangan dicampur.
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *mengurangi, meningkatkan, melatih* otomatis sama bentuknya. Dalam bahasa Inggris, pilih bentuk untuk bagian pertama lalu tiru.

pairs.en: The project aims to reduce costs, improve quality and train staff.
pairs.id: Proyek ini bertujuan mengurangi biaya, meningkatkan kualitas, dan melatih staf.

pairs.en: The project focuses on reducing costs, improving quality and training staff.
pairs.id: Proyek ini berfokus pada pengurangan biaya, peningkatan kualitas, dan pelatihan staf.

steps.title: Pasangan yang sejajar
steps.text: Kedua bagian sebuah pasangan juga harus sama bentuknya.
steps.body: Setelah **both … and**, **either … or**, **neither … nor**, **not only … but also**, kedua bagiannya sejajar: *both demanding and well paid* ✓, bukan *both demanding and pays well* ✗. Perbandingan dengan *than* juga: *faster than driving*, bukan *than to drive*.

examples.id: Pekerjaan itu menuntut sekaligus bergaji bagus. (dua kata sifat)

examples.en: She not only wrote the code but also tested it.
examples.id: Dia tidak hanya menulis kodenya, tetapi juga mengujinya. (dua kata kerja)

examples.en: We can either meet in Bandung or talk online.
examples.id: Kita bisa bertemu di Bandung atau bicara secara online. (dua kata kerja)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pak Hasan sedang menulis tujuan sebuah program baru. Periksa setiap bagian setelah 'aims to'.

question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang struktur paralelnya benar?
options: The programme aims to support small farmers, cutting food waste and to create local jobs.
The programme aims to support small farmers, to cut food waste and creating local jobs.
The programme aims to support small farmers, cut food waste and create local jobs.
question.explanation: Satu *to* di awal, lalu tiga kata kerja dasar: *support, cut, create*. Dua kalimat lainnya mencampur to + kata kerja dengan bentuk -ing, jadi daftarnya kehilangan pola.

steps.title: Urai tumpukan kata benda
steps.text: Satu kata inti, dan hanya sedikit kata di depannya.
steps.body:
**Ulasan (C1):** noun phrase punya satu **kata inti** (head); kata kerjanya mengikuti kata inti itu.
**Noun stack** menumpuk banyak kata benda di depan kata inti: *the government new rural school teacher training funding policy* ✗
**Cara mengurai:** cari kata intinya (biasanya kata benda terakhir: *policy*), taruh pemilik dan kata sifat di depannya, lalu pindahkan detailnya ke belakang dengan *on / for / in / of* atau satu klausa relatif.
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** jangan membalik urutan bahasa Indonesia jadi tumpukan, dan jangan ubah setiap *yang* menjadi *which is*.

pairs.en: the government's new policy on funding teacher training in rural schools
pairs.id: kebijakan baru pemerintah tentang pendanaan pelatihan guru di sekolah-sekolah pedesaan

pairs.en: the hospital's plan to recruit more night-shift nurses
pairs.id: rencana rumah sakit untuk merekrut lebih banyak perawat shift malam

steps.title: Cari versi yang paling jelas
steps.text: Laporan Bu Ani menyebut 'the city council new street food vendor licence fee'.

question.prompt: Mana cara paling jelas untuk menulis 'the city council new street food vendor licence fee' dalam laporan?
options: the city council's new licence fee for street food vendors
the new fee of the licence of the vendors of street food of the city council
the fee which is new which is for the licence which street food vendors need from the city council
question.explanation: Kata inti = **fee**. Pemilik dan kata sifat di depannya (*the city council's new licence fee*), orangnya di belakang (*for street food vendors*). Pilihan kedua adalah rantai *of*, pilihan ketiga terjemahan *yang … yang …*: keduanya mengubur kata intinya.

steps.title: Empat jenis ambiguitas
steps.text: Bisakah kalimatmu dibaca dengan dua cara? Ini penyebab yang paling sering.
steps.body:
**1. Dangling modifier:** *Walking into the office, the computer was already on* ✗ → *…, **I** saw that the computer was already on*.
**2. only/almost salah tempat:** keduanya membatasi kata tepat sesudahnya. *We **almost lost** every client* (tidak ada yang hilang) ≠ *We lost **almost every** client* (sebagian besar hilang).
**3. Kata ganti tidak jelas:** *When the manager met the consultant, **she** said …* Siapa? Ulangi kata bendanya.
**4. Frasa menempel ke dua kata:** *I saw the man **with the binoculars**.* Teropong siapa? → *Using binoculars, I saw the man.*

pairs.id: Hanya Rina yang menandatangani kontrak itu.
Rina hanya menandatangani kontrak itu, bukan dokumen lain.

pairs.en: When the manager met the consultant, the consultant said the budget was too small.
pairs.id: Saat manajer bertemu konsultan, konsultan itulah yang bilang anggarannya terlalu kecil.

steps.title: Laptop siapa?
steps.text: Budi dan Dimas sama-sama laki-laki, jadi 'his' bisa menunjuk ke salah satunya.

question.prompt: Laptop Dimas-lah yang rusak. Kalimat mana yang mengatakannya dengan jelas?
options: Budi phoned Dimas because his laptop had crashed.
Dimas's laptop had crashed, so Budi phoned him.
Budi phoned Dimas because of his crashed laptop.
question.explanation: Pada kalimat pertama dan ketiga, *his* bisa berarti milik Budi atau milik Dimas. Kalimat kedua menyebut pemiliknya (*Dimas's laptop*), dan *him* hanya bisa berarti Dimas, karena Budi yang menelepon.

steps.title: Taruh almost di tempatnya
steps.text: almost membatasi kata tepat sesudahnya.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Dia (memang) mengirim laporan itu ke hampir semua mitra.
question.solution: She sent the report to almost every partner.
question.explanation: *almost every partner* = hampir semua mitra, dan laporannya benar-benar dikirim. *She almost sent the report to every partner* berarti dia sama sekali tidak jadi mengirimnya.

steps.title: Kalimat panjang: susun atau pecah
steps.text: Satu kalimat bisa memuat empat klausa, asal disusun dengan baik.
steps.body:
Klausa partisip + **klausa utama** + klausa relatif + alasan, semuanya dalam satu kalimat (lihat kartunya).
**Supaya jelas:** subjek utama dan kata kerjanya muncul awal dan berdekatan; setiap klausa tambahan di samping hal yang dijelaskannya; informasi panjang dan baru di akhir; **klausa paralel** untuk ide yang sejajar (*why …, what … and how …*).
**Pecah** kalau ada dua pesan utama atau pembaca terlalu lama menunggu kata kerja.
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** rantai panjang *yang … dan … sehingga … di mana …*. *di mana* hanya menjadi *where* untuk tempat atau situasi.

pairs.en: Having reviewed the figures, the board approved the budget, which had been cut by 10%, because sales had risen.
pairs.id: Setelah meninjau angka-angkanya, dewan menyetujui anggaran, yang sudah dipotong 10%, karena penjualan naik.

steps.title: Seimbangkan klausanya
steps.text: Setelah peluncuran tertunda dua bulan, dewan minta laporan. Perhatikan tiga hal yang harus dijelaskan.

question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang klausanya tetap paralel?
options: The report should explain why the launch was delayed, our lessons and how to avoid delays in future.
The report should explain why the launch was delayed, what we learnt and how we will avoid delays in future.
The report should explain why the launch was delayed, what we learnt and avoiding delays in future.
question.explanation: Ketiganya adalah **klausa wh-** dengan subjek dan kata kerjanya sendiri: *why … was delayed, what we learnt, how we will avoid*. Pilihan pertama menyelipkan noun phrase (*our lessons*) dan *how to*; pilihan ketiga diakhiri bentuk -ing.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman. Periksa ini sebelum mengirim laporan.
